usage: icebath desktop [-h] [--source] [--build-only] [--fake-boot] [--ignore-existing]
                       [--icebath-root ICEBATH_ROOT] [--cwd CWD] [--skip-build] [--local]
                       [--force-build] [--setup-tcc-identity] [--identity IDENTITY]
                       [--install-apparmor-profile] [--close-preview]

Launch the Icebath Electron desktop app. By default this installs workspace Node dependencies,
builds the current OS's unpacked Electron app, then launches that packaged artifact.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --source              Launch via `electron .` against apps/desktop/dist instead of the packaged
                        app
  --build-only          Build the desktop app but do not launch it (used by the installer's
                        --update flow)
  --fake-boot           Enable deterministic desktop boot delays for validating startup UI
  --ignore-existing     Skip the installed Icebath runtime (~/.icebath/icebath-agent) so no local
                        backend starts and Desktop offers connect or install instead. --icebath-
                        root and the bundled runtime still win; a runtime installed during this
                        launch is used.
  --icebath-root ICEBATH_ROOT
                        Override the Icebath source root used by Desktop (sets
                        ICEBATH_DESKTOP_ICEBATH_ROOT)
  --cwd CWD             Initial project directory for Desktop chat sessions (sets
                        ICEBATH_DESKTOP_CWD)
  --skip-build          Skip npm install/package and launch the existing unpacked app from
                        apps/desktop/release
  --local               Show the local-models UI in the desktop app (models pane, quickstart,
                        picker rows)
  --force-build         Force a full rebuild even if the content stamp matches
  --setup-tcc-identity  macOS only: create/import a self-signed code-signing certificate in the
                        login keychain and point desktop.macos_signing_identity at it, then re-
                        sign the packaged app. Makes macOS TCC grants (Full Disk Access,
                        Accessibility, Files and Folders, microphone) survive rebuilds with a
                        certificate-anchored identity. Idempotent — safe to re-run after updates.
  --identity IDENTITY   Certificate name to create/use for --setup-tcc-identity (default: Icebath
                        Local Signing)
  --install-apparmor-profile
                        Linux only: install an AppArmor profile (sudo) that lets the packaged app
                        use Chromium's user-namespace sandbox on hosts with
                        kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 (Ubuntu 23.10+), then exit.
                        Survives rebuilds of the same checkout.
  --close-preview       Close the preview pane and exit its fullscreen (out-of-band escape hatch
                        when the pane captured all input)
